An item's document read on its own, as the overlay draws it (F28): its
timeline entry, but that a document done by Done reads as Done fixed it

close_starts_work.description: Whether a person's close of it on the page starts Pilot's work, as the record stands at this read, which the button that closes it says under the mouse (F59.3): an item a session of Pilot's own added, but a notice, its close placing the job after it; a registered document whose run's turn has ended and whose other documents are all closed, its close continuing the run. Read at every read, never stored; false once done, and while the project is archived

concept.description: Whether the latest save of its text is held, its text shown as last published until a parseable save arrives (F78)

debriefs.description: A debrief's notice's work items, whose debriefs it carries, in timeline order, each as its work item stands at this read (F26.13); null for every other kind

for_user.description: The person it is for (F107); null for everyone

The latest placed where several stand on it, a Retry over the job it retries, a wait's latest run; never a withdrawn job, nor the setup. Null where none shows

pilots_work.description: What Pilot does on it while it is Pilot's (F13.7; DB 296): a registered document awaiting its read, under its pass or its clarification, or with every open block held; it waits on no person. Null while it is the person's or done, and for every other item

examples: Three tents compared; the dome wins on weight.

text.description: The text the read is drawn from, as written: its front matter, its prose and its blocks; as Done fixed it where Done did, else as last published. Null for the opening and for a registered document with no text

word_count.title: Word Count

words.description: The opening's words, verbatim; null for every other item
words.title: Words

work.description: A work item's Session, which the SSE event `work_moved` carries as it moves; null for every other kind

get.description:
A raster image is served inline as its type, text other than HTML inline as plain text; anything else, an SVG and HTML among it, as a download of `application/octet-stream`, whatever type it was stored with. The type is never sniffed.

Returns:     200: The bytes     401: No one is signed in     403: The caller lacks the editor role     404: No attachment has the id
get.summary: Stream an attachment's bytes, with its file's name and its length.

get.description:
Exchanges authorization code for tokens and sets access token cookie.

Query Parameters:     code: Authorization code from OIDC provider     state: CSRF token from OIDC provider

Returns:     302: Redirect to original redirect URL with access token cookie set     400: Invalid or missing callback parameters     401: Token exchange failed
get.summary: Handle OIDC callback after user authorization.

get.description:
Generates authorization URL and redirects to OIDC provider. PKCE state is encrypted into the OAuth state parameter. The ``redirect_uri`` is the callback on the origin the request came in on, so the app signs in on every hostname it is served on (each one registered at the IdP).

Query Parameters:     redirect: Path to redirect to after successful login (required)

Returns:     302: Redirect to OIDC provider authorization endpoint     400: Missing or invalid redirect parameter
get.summary: Initiate OIDC login flow with PKCE.

get.description:
Clears access token cookie and redirects to OIDC provider's logout endpoint to terminate the session at the IdP level.

Query Parameters:     redirect: Path to redirect to after logout (default: /)

Returns:     302: Redirect to OIDC logout endpoint (or direct redirect if OIDC disabled)     400: Invalid redirect parameter
get.summary: Log out current user.

get.description:
This endpoint is @public, so the request hook resolves the caller (refreshing an expired access token) without answering 401 itself, and the handler answers 401 when no one is signed in. A caller with none of the app's roles gets 403 from the hook. With OIDC disabled, the caller is the local admin.

Returns:     200: User information     401: No valid token provided or token invalid     403: User authenticated but has none of the app's roles
get.summary: Get current authenticated user information.

put.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

Each answer is the call's outcome, and all but the first leave the record as it was:

- 204: each File the call names holds the class it names; only those   that differed were written. A File the call does not name keeps its   class. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none. - 400: the call does not validate, every fault named at once: the fields   that are not the call's shape, or, in `error`, a File given twice, one   Pilot does not hold, or a class the labeller does not declare. The   same call is refused again. - 413: the body is over `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`. The same call is refused   again.
put.summary: The classes the labeller gave Files Pilot holds, each by its Repository's name and its path. One call, one transaction.

post.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

Each answer is the call's outcome, and all but the first leave the record as it was:

- 204: Pilot holds every commit as read. One completes the Commit held   from the call that made it whose hash it starts with, else the one   whose subject it has and whose call its author's time lies within the   hour of; a hash wins over a subject, and a Commit is tied once. One   that completes none is a Commit no Transcript made. A commit Pilot   holds as read already changes nothing. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none. - 400: the call does not validate, every fault named at once: the fields   that are not the call's shape, or, in `error`, a Repository Pilot does   not hold, a commit given twice or a file one commit changes twice. The   same call is refused again. - 413: the body is over `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`. The same call is refused   again.
post.summary: What a read of one Repository's history gave: commits Pilot lacked, each with its whole hash, its author's time, its subject and its lines per file, and when they were read. One call, one transaction.

get.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

- 200: each File by its Repository's name and its path, in that order;   none where none is asked for. - 400: `unclassed` is not a boolean. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none.

parameters.description: True for the Files with no class; false for every File
parameters.name: unclassed

get.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

- 200: every transcript Pilot holds, a main thread's and a sub-agent's,   each by its `session_id` and `agent_id` with its last publication's   `file_size`, `file_modified_at` and collector's version, which are what   an appended publication of it builds on, its `replayed_size`, and the   labeller's version and stamp its labels were written under, none for   one published with no labelling; every conversation a Session of   Pilot's ran, collected or not, with what the labeller is handed with   it, its Sessions with their Holds and Turns and the Documents they   put; and the walk's two settings, `COLLECTOR_WALK_INTERVAL_SECONDS` and   `COLLECTOR_SETTLING_SECONDS`. A transcript the home has and the answer   lacks, or holds at another size, time or version, is one to publish;   one whose `replayed_size` is short of its `file_size`, its file   unchanged for the settling time, is published whole once. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none.
get.summary: Pilot's inventory, which a collector asks for as each walk starts: what Pilot holds, whole, for the walk to compare the home against.

post.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks. The body is the transcript as its file stands, read whole, or, with `appended`, what a file that grew holds from a boundary on.

Each answer is the call's outcome, and all but the first leave the record as it was:

- 204: Pilot holds the transcript as the call says. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. No call of this collector's is taken   until its bearer is the server's. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none. No call is taken until the collector speaks a   version in the range. - 400: the call does not validate, every fault named at once: the fields   that are not the call's shape, or, in `error`, what in the call   contradicts itself or the record's rules for a transcript. The same   call is refused again; the collector's other transcripts are not. - 409, with the `code` `PUBLICATION_NOT_APPENDABLE`: an appended call   does not continue what Pilot holds of the transcript, the reasons in   `error`: Pilot does not hold it at the size and time and under the   collector's version the call builds on, holds no row at a place before   the boundary's, holds from there on, or before, what the call does   not carry so, or holds at the boundary's `launch`, `prompt` or   `compaction` another one than the call's first, told by its time; or   its `labelling` does not continue the labels Pilot holds: they are   under another stamp or none, or another major of the labeller's   version, or its first Segment is neither the one the Call before the   boundary falls in nor the next. The collector publishes the   transcript whole. - 409, with the `code` `TRANSCRIPT_NOT_ADOPTABLE`: the call names a   `group` for a transcript a session of Pilot's ran, which no adopted   project adopts. The same call is refused again, and the call without   its `group` is taken. - 409, with the `code` `NO_SERVICE_USER`: the call names a `group` no   project holds yet, and the stage has no service user to make its   adopted project. The same call is taken once the stage has one. - 413: the body is over `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`. The same call is refused   again.
post.summary: A collector's publication of one transcript, a main thread's or one sub-agent's: one call, one transaction.

get.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

- 200: each Repository by name, with the whole hash of every Commit a   read of it gave. A commit of its history not among them is one Pilot   lacks, to be read; a Repository with none is read whole. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none.
get.summary: Every Repository Pilot holds, the cursor of a collector's reads of their histories from its clones of the mirror.

put.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

Each answer is the call's outcome, and all but the first leave the record as it was:

- 204: Pilot holds every list and every nesting as the call declares   them. A value or a nesting the call no longer declares is gone where   no row names it, and kept where one does, a value with no place. The   collector's values of Event Kind and Context Part Kind stand as they   are. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none. - 400: the call does not validate, every fault named at once: the fields   that are not the call's shape, a list the record has no place for among   them, or, in `error`, what in the call contradicts itself: a code or a   place given twice in a list, an Event Kind another entity records, or   a nesting given twice or naming a Work Unit Kind the call does not   declare. The same call is refused again. - 413: the body is over `MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB`. The same call is refused   again.
put.summary: The labeller's vocabularies, whole, as the labeller declares them: every list a label takes its value from, by the reference entity it fills, each value with its code, its name, its line, its place and the fact about its category where it has one; the Work Unit Kinds' nestings; and the labeller's version that declared them. One call, one transaction.

post.description:
Headers: `Authorization`, `Bearer` and the setting `COLLECTOR_TOKEN`; `X-Pilot-Collector-Protocol`, the protocol version the collector speaks.

- 204: the server stamped the walk at this moment, which the readiness   check `collector` reads. Where a transcript was published since the   walk before ended, every person's connections are sent one   `collection_changed` event, its `as_of` this walk's end; a walk that   published nothing raises none. A walk's end that does not arrive   raises nothing either: what it would have announced, the next walk's   end announces. - 401: the call does not carry the collector's bearer, and every call   while `COLLECTOR_TOKEN` is empty. - 426, with the range `{min, max}`: the call names a protocol version   outside it, or none.
post.summary: A walk's end, which a collector tells once per walk, after its last publication, whether the walk published anything or not. The call has no body.

post.description:
Create project opens a draft: its slug the draft's, its handbook born empty, its opening first on the timeline with the draft's copy and the material Pilot attached, its definition chat closed, its folder moved once committed. Finish also turns auto pilot off, resumes a paused project, stops the project's sessions and closes its open items unanswered; Archive stops the sessions too, and nothing of the project starts after either. Reopen leaves auto pilot off. A resume lets the project's held starts go on. Auto pilot turned on with `answer_confirmations` answers Yes, as the caller's through `autopilot`, every open confirmation it would have taken, each answer doing what a person's does.

Returns:     201: The project's head, with its new standing     400: The kind is not one a person makes, or `answer_confirmations`         goes with a kind other than `autopilot_on`     401: No one is signed in     403: The caller lacks the editor role     404: No project has the id     409: The caller has not chosen a handle, or the project's standing         does not allow the change, or Create project's draft does not,         or an answer's job finds no controller configured
post.summary: Change the project's standing, as the signed-in person, now.

post.description:
The allowance's target is the latest reading's week share plus the allowance, at most the second limit; run-out's is the wall. The overrule holds until a reading reaches its target or shows the share lower than the one before, or a stale reading's week is a minute past its reset; meanwhile the week's halt holds no work item, and every person's connections hear the conditions once it is made.

get.description: `hello` first, `{protocol: {min, max}, manifest_hash}`; then a `change`, `{path, hash}`, for every tree hash that moved once its transaction has committed, and a `manifest`, `{}`, whenever the set of syncing projects changed; a heartbeat comment after `SYNC_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS` idle. No `id:` field: the sidecar's hashes are its cursor. Ends on shutdown, and when the stream falls too far behind. Refused with 401, 403 or 426, and answered 502, as every sync call is.

put.description:
Headers: `X-Pilot-Base-Hash`, the hash the sidecar last synced for the path, or `none`; `X-Pilot-Session`, the Session that held the write lock of the path's project folder as the sidecar read the file, left out when none held it: the save is that Session's when it is a brain session of the path's project, and no Session's otherwise. The body is the file's bytes, at most `SYNC_PUT_MAX_BYTES`.

Answers 204 when the file needs no change, 200 with the bytes it must now hold when it does; either with `X-Pilot-Hash`, the hash the file holds once answered, and `X-Pilot-Faults`, the count of Save Errors the save raised on the path, and `X-Pilot-Stale: true` when the base hash was not the path's tree hash. 404 for a path of no syncing project.

post.description: `youtrack`'s credential is the header `X-YouTrack-Token`, the instance's webhook token; its body the Webhook Triggers app's `issueUpdated`. Answers 200 with how many waits fired, none for a delivery that reports no change of State or matches no open card wait; 401 for a delivery without the token, and every delivery while none is configured; 400 for a body the tracker's adapter cannot read; 404 for no such tracker.
post.summary: A delivery of `tracker`'s, `youtrack` the one there is: the card waits the change of state it reports matches fire inside the request (F136.2).
